newsitem.title: USA: Used-home sales drop in December but set 1996 record.
newsitem.headline: Used-home sales drop in December but set 1996 record.

text.p: Sales of existing homes dropped steeply in December, the National Association of Realtors said Monday, but still set a record for the full year.

The real estate lobby group said sales of existing, or used, homes fell 3.5 percent last month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.87 million from a revised 4.01 million in November. The total was much lower than the 4-million-unit monthly sales rate forecast by Wall Street economists.

But for the full year 1996, sales of existing homes were up strongly, by 7.5 percent to a 4.09 million, a record pace that the group attributed to the economy's steady expansion without generating strong inflationary pressures and to mortgage rates that were low by historical standards.

"The soft landing of the economy and favourable interest rates contributed to affordable conditions in both the first-time buyer and move-up homebuyer markets," said John Tuccillo, chief economist for the Realtors' association.
Previously, they said November sales of existing homes were at an annual rate of 4.04 million but that figure was revised down to 4.01 million.

Despite the bigger-than-expected drop in sales during December, the home-sales market remained relatively strong. Last month's sales rate of 3.87 million was the same as that recorded in December 1995, just before the sales pace began to accelerate throughout much of 1996.

The sales rate topped 4-million-a-year in eight out of 12 months last year. The real estate group said the December slowdown was not surprising after "months of frenetic activity" in the buying and selling of used homes.
"In general, the market is as strong now as it was a year ago," Realtors' association president Russell Booth said, adding "Consumers often avoid moving in the winter months."
Mortgage rates for a 30-year loan during December averaged 7.60 percent, down from 7.62 percent in November, but up moderately from 7.20 percent posted a year earlier in december 1995.
